blocks.content: Recent technological advancements have significantly transformed the field of computing. Modern computer systems now integrate advanced technologies that improve data processing, automation, connectivity, and intelligent decision-making. Some of the most important developments in modern computing include Cloud Computing, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT), and Big Data.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Cloud Computing encompasses distinct characteristics, deployment types, and service models (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS).
Artificial Intelligence (AI) focuses on machine learning models, various AI types, and practical real-world applications.
Internet of Things (IoT) integrates physical hardware components and software to enable smart device connectivity.
Big Data is characterized by the 5Vs: Volume, Velocity, Variety, Veracity, and Value.

blocks.content: Cloud Computing refers to the delivery of computing services such as servers, storage, databases, networking, software, and analytics over the Internet (the cloud). Instead of owning physical hardware or data centers, organizations can access these resources on demand.

items: On-demand self-service – Users can access computing resources without human interaction.
Broad network access – Services are accessible via the Internet from multiple devices.
Resource pooling – Multiple users share computing resources.
Rapid elasticity – Resources can be scaled up or down quickly.
Measured service – Usage is monitored and billed based on consumption.

cells: Services provided over the public Internet by third-party providers.
Dedicated cloud infrastructure used by a single organization.
Combination of public and private cloud environments.
Shared cloud infrastructure used by several organizations.
Provides virtualized computing resources such as servers and storage.

blocks.content: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a branch of computer science that enables machines to simulate human intelligence. AI systems can learn from data, recognize patterns, make decisions, and perform tasks that normally require human intelligence.

cells: AI designed to perform a specific task.
AI capable of performing any intellectual task a human can perform.

items: Voice assistants (Siri, Alexa, Google Assistant).
Self-driving cars.
Medical diagnosis systems.
Recommendation systems used by Netflix and Amazon.
Fraud detection in banking.

blocks.content: The Internet of Things (IoT) refers to the network of physical devices connected to the Internet that collect and exchange data.

items: Sensors – Collect data from the environment.
Connectivity – Devices connect to the Internet.
Data Processing – Data is analyzed and processed.
User Interface – Allows users to interact with devices.
Smart homes (smart lights, smart thermostats).
Wearable devices (fitness trackers, smart watches).
Smart cities.
Industrial automation.
Healthcare monitoring systems.

blocks.content: Big Data refers to extremely large datasets that cannot be easily processed using traditional data processing techniques.

items: Identify and differentiate the 5Vs of Big Data: Volume, Velocity, Variety, Veracity, and Value.
